excerpt: Supabase Auth makes it easy to implement authentication and authorization in your app.
You can connect this data to your own tables using triggers and foreign key references.
The Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with [RLS policies](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security).
Use Clerk, Auth0, Firebase Auth, Cognito, or WorkOS JWTs with Supabase APIs.
You can use Supabase Auth as a standalone product, but it's also built to integrate with the Supabase ecosystem.
Add a second factor to user sign-in with TOTP or phone.
Customize Auth behavior with Postgres functions at key lifecycle points.
Add Single Sign-On for enterprise applications with SAML 2.0.
Sign up and sign in users with a Magic Link or email OTP instead of a password.
Control session lifetime, refresh tokens, and multi-device sign-in behavior.
Create a Supabase client for SSR frameworks like Next.js and SvelteKit.
To add a provider that isn't listed, use [Custom OAuth/OIDC Providers](/docs/guides/auth/custom-oauth-providers).
You can use the provider token and provider refresh token returned to make API calls to the OAuth provider.
You can use a [Custom Access Token Hook](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) to add, remove or change claims present in the token.
If you are already using Supabase Auth, when a user is signed in, their access token JWT is automatically managed and sent for you with every API call.
If you wish to send a JWT from a Third-Party Auth provider, or one you made yourself by using a JWT signing key you imported, you can pass it to the client library using the `accessToken` option.

A password must contain at least one character of each set to be accepted.
If refresh token rotation is enabled, auth will automatically detect malicious attempts to reuse a revoked refresh token.

Self-hosted Supabase **does not phone home or collect any telemetry**.
Use `-y` to run non-interactively with default values.

A React Native developer who had already built Google sign-in said 'Supabase makes auth incredibly easy.' However, it took them a while to work out the auth flow with Expo/RN, and they ended up using Expo AuthSession. The only existing RN guide covers email/password, and the OAuth flow is more convoluted, so they want an RN OAuth template or getting-started guide.

A developer/entrepreneur said they 'can't advocate Supabase enough.' They praised the platform's openness and elegance, said it leaves them feeling secure, and said Supabase has 'nailed AuthN.' They asked which enterprise-grade AuthZ provider (e.g., Cerbos or Casbin) pairs best with it.

A user new to implementing multi-tenant SSO was excited about Supabase's SAML SSO. They said other SaaS options like Auth0 were complicated and overwhelmed them. They were unclear whether OIDC-based SSO is or will be supported.
'I want, want, want to use Supabase - I yearn for a first party SDK for iOS.'

A user wants to use Supabase Auth itself as an IdP/SAML provider, so back-office tools or multiple Supabase projects can share one auth system. They are currently building something like this on top of Supabase for work themselves.

A Supabase fan said session encryption is easy with cookie auth since you provide the storage adapter. They suggested reported random logouts likely come from not refreshing the JWT, and have had no issue. They built a Rails app that interoperates with Supabase's RLS, and called copying user data to a public table trivial, not lock-in.

While evaluating auth options for a new project, a user said they were 'similarly disappointed with the quality of Supabase's auth offering considering all the praise I consistently see for Supabase on HN.'

A user considering Supabase for their next project said they were 'quite surprised at the auth issues apparent in Supabase considering the funding.' They asked others for good or bad experiences with Supabase Auth.

A user had put effort into building an app that anonymous users could try while still enforcing RLS policies. They said Supabase's new anonymous sign-ins 'would have made the whole thing heaps easier.'
